headline: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $60,000 After Two-Year Low
deck: Reports put the recovery at more than 8% after its lowest level in two years.
body: Bitcoin traded at $60,192.07 at 10:16 a.m. ET on Saturday, up about 2.14%, Investing.com reported. [E1]
Investing.com reported that Bitcoin had broken below $57,742 on Friday, its lowest level since September 2024. [E2]
At $60,064.86, Bitcoin had climbed back above $60,000 and was more than 9% above an early low of $55,130, CoinDesk reported; it called that low the weakest since September 2024. [E3]

CoinDesk put Bitcoin near $60,300 in the early afternoon U.S. time, up 1.5% over 24 hours, and, citing CoinGlass data, said about $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions were wiped out in that period, including $1.3 billion in bets on rising prices. [E4][E5]
Friday’s selloff cleared the largest cluster on Glassnode’s heat map of estimated Bitcoin-futures liquidations, CoinDesk reported. [E6]
Glassnode said the closures removed “a large source of forced selling” below the market, CoinDesk reported. [E7]

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost described the selloff as “extreme capitulation,” and said Bitcoin holders realised more than $11.3 billion in losses over seven days, about eight times the gains booked in that period, according to CoinDesk. [E8][E9]
MarketScreener reported that Bitcoin rose more than 8% to around $59,952 on Saturday after reaching its lowest level in two years earlier that day. [E10]
Bitcoin briefly crossed $60,000 at around 8:30 a.m. EST, or 1330 GMT, MarketScreener reported. [E11]

MarketScreener reported an earlier Bitcoin price of $55,251.60, its lowest in two years, and said stretched valuations in artificial-intelligence stocks had rattled investors and weighed on other risk assets. [E12]
This follows the paper’s Friday report that Bitcoin fell 5.10% to $55,830, its lowest level since September 2024. [E13]
